newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Thomson-CSF upgrading Uzbek air traffic control.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF upgrading Uzbek air traffic control.

text.p: France's Thomson CSF will soon begin the second and final phase of an upgrade of Uzbekistan's air traffic control system, a company official said on Monday.
"When the project is completed at the end of 1998, the system will meet all international flight safety requirements," the official told Reuters without naming a starting date for the second phase.
The former Soviet republic is making a bid to become a major Central Asian hub for international air traffic.
The $17.3 million contract signed between Ukbekistan's national air carrier and Thomson includes the installation of two radar sites in the towns of Nukus and Termez.
The official said the systems would be integrated with the air traffic control system in the capital Tashkent, on which Thomson carried out a $37.7 million upgrade last year.

He said Thomson, Uzbek airlines, Uzbekistan's space research agency and U.S. company California Microwave Inc are considering a joint venture to put in place a satellite navigation system which would cover the entire republic.
